issue_context.summary: Always on Top produces no visible or audible activation on Parsec even with PowerToys elevated; the reporter already supplied the target window's style report.
known_information: Reported versions are PowerToys 0.81.0 and Parsec 150-94a.
The MTY_Window attachment has WS_VISIBLE, WS_CAPTION and WS_THICKFRAME; it is not WS_CHILD, WS_EX_TOOLWINDOW or cloaked.
The window is on the current virtual desktop and is not already topmost.
The issue is open and unassigned.
inferences: No activation feedback is consistent with the command never arriving or returning before pinning; it does not prove either.
Generic app-compatibility labels and bot matches do not establish an external-only defect.

actions.label: Trace local shortcut while Parsec is focused

reproduce.title: Separate input capture from Always on Top guard exits
reproduce.version_requirement: Current PowerToys and Parsec; compare Parsec 150-94a and PowerToys 0.81.0 if available in an isolated test.
prerequisites: A Parsec test client and optional remote test session; enable sound/border for the test.
Inspect user exclusions and game-mode blocking without overriding them silently.
steps: 1. Verify the configured shortcut pins a normal local application.
2. Focus the Parsec client while idle and press the shortcut; repeat during a remote session.
3. Trace whether PowerToys receives the hotkey and which HWND reaches ProcessCommand.
4. Record the game-mode and exclusion decisions, then the SetWindowPos result if reached.
5. Test an alternative configured local shortcut to distinguish remote key capture; restore settings afterward.
reproduce.expected_result: An unblocked local command pins the intended window. If no local command arrives, record the input-routing limitation rather than weakening window filtering.
